title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #2

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What are guide words? (1 mark)
   A. The longest words in the book
   B. The first and last words on a dictionary page
   C. The words on the cover
   D. Words that rhyme

2. Where would you find facts about elephants? (1 mark)
   A. A form
   B. A junior encyclopaedia
   C. A timetable
   D. A calendar

3. What is a signature? (1 mark)
   A. Your telephone number
   B. Your name written in your own handwriting
   C. Your date of birth
   D. Your grade

4. Target sounds: Which word has the sound /ɜː/? (1 mark)
   A. girl
   B. toy
   C. party
   D. five

5. To make the /l/ sound, the tip of the tongue (1 mark)
   A. stays far from the roof of the mouth and curls back
   B. touches the ridge behind the top front teeth
   C. touches the bottom lip
   D. touches the top lip

6. What should you do before you read a story? (1 mark)
   A. Read the title and look at the pictures
   B. Read the last page only
   C. Close the book
   D. Write the answers

7. Which pair is a minimal pair for /e/ and /eɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. pin, bin
   B. pat, bat
   C. ten, den
   D. let, late

8. What do we say when a friend wins a prize? (1 mark)
   A. Good night
   B. I beg your pardon
   C. Excuse me
   D. Congratulations

9. To scan a text means to (1 mark)
   A. copy the text
   B. draw pictures
   C. read every word slowly
   D. look quickly for one fact

10. Which closing is suitable for a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Dear Sir,
   B. To whom it may concern,
   C. Yours faithfully,
   D. Yours lovingly,

11. What is fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Reading only one word
   B. Reading smoothly with few stops
   C. Reading very loudly
   D. Not reading

12. Which material gives you news? (1 mark)
   A. A newspaper
   B. A story book
   C. A map key
   D. A dictionary

13. What is the comparative form of 'tall'? (1 mark)
   A. more tall
   B. tallr
   C. taller
   D. tallest

14. Narratives: Which sentence has a simile? (1 mark)
   A. Bread is food.
   B. The bread was as soft as a pillow.
   C. We ate bread.
   D. The bread was soft.

15. To compose an email means to (1 mark)
   A. delete a message
   B. answer a phone
   C. print a message
   D. write a new message

16. What is a rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. Words with opposite meanings
   B. Words that end with the same sound
   C. Words that start with the same letter
   D. Words with the same meaning

17. Choose the correct -ing form of 'lie' (to rest flat). (1 mark)
   A. liing
   B. lieing
   C. lying
   D. lyeing

18. Which sentence is in the present progressive? (1 mark)
   A. The teacher marks our books.
   B. The teacher had marked our books.
   C. The teacher is marking our books.
   D. The teacher marked our books.

19. Which is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. The goat is a runner.
   B. The goat ran like the wind.
   C. The goat ran quickly.
   D. The goat was fast.

20. Which sentence would best begin a narrative about a farm visit? (1 mark)
   A. Last Saturday, my class visited a farm near our school.
   B. The farm is nice.
   C. I like cows.
   D. Farms grow food.

21. Which of these is a nonverbal cue that shows confidence? (1 mark)
   A. Turning your back
   B. Standing straight and looking at your audience
   C. Looking at the floor
   D. Hiding your face

22. Which word in the story means 'said no to doing something'? (1 mark)
   A. noticed
   B. refused
   C. nodded
   D. smiled

23. In 'The Barber's New Blade', why does the barber use a new blade for each customer? (1 mark)
   A. The blade is red
   B. Sharing blades can pass germs through blood
   C. Customers like blades
   D. New blades are cheaper

24. Which sentence should end with a full stop, not a question mark? (1 mark)
   A. Are you ready
   B. Where is the clinic
   C. She asked where the clinic was.
   D. What is her name

25. Why should water from rivers be boiled before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. It is too clear
   B. It is too cold
   C. It may contain germs
   D. It tastes sweet

26. Which sentence uses 'nor' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. She has no soap, nor does she have water.
   B. She has no soap, nor water has she.
   C. She has no soap, nor she does have water.
   D. She has no soap nor does have water she.

27. Which conjunction joins two negative ideas? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. so
   C. nor
   D. and

28. What should you do to listen fluently to a speech? (1 mark)
   A. Draw during the speech
   B. Face the speaker and listen for the main points
   C. Talk to a friend
   D. Look at your phone

29. Which is the best answer to 'When does the match begin?' (1 mark)
   A. It is mine.
   B. On the field.
   C. The referee.
   D. At ten o'clock.

30. Which word has a double r? (1 mark)
   A. necessary
   B. library
   C. tomorrow
   D. beautiful

31. Which is the correct spelling of the word for a person who is not just an acquaintance? (1 mark)
   A. frind
   B. freind
   C. friend
   D. frend

32. Which of these helps you speak fluently? (1 mark)
   A. Never looking at the audience
   B. Speaking as fast as possible
   C. Mumbling
   D. Practising what you want to say

33. What is rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of the page
   B. The number of lines
   C. The title
   D. The beat in the words

34. How should you read a poem with rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. Whisper every line
   B. Read as fast as you can
   C. Tap the beat and stress the strong syllables
   D. Skip the rhymes

35. When I arrived, the bus had left. Which happened first? (1 mark)
   A. I arrived.
   B. The bus left.
   C. Neither happened.
   D. Both together.

36. Which sentence uses the correct form of the verb 'go' with the present perfect? (1 mark)
   A. They have go to the river.
   B. They have went to the river.
   C. They has gone to the river.
   D. They have gone to the river.

37. What does 'scanning' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Copying the text
   B. Looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number
   C. Drawing a picture
   D. Reading every word slowly

38. Which preposition completes: 'She put the coins ____ the tin.'? (1 mark)
   A. into
   B. between
   C. opposite
   D. beside

39. Which is the correct spelling of the word for a person who keeps money records? (1 mark)
   A. accountent
   B. acountant
   C. acounttant
   D. accountant

40. What is the -ing form of 'stop'? (1 mark)
   A. stoppping
   B. stopping
   C. stoping
   D. stopeing

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain how a word wheel can help you make new words. Give an example with the ending -oy. (4 marks)

42. Explain how you can tell b from d when you write. (2 marks)

43. Cross out the silent letter in each word: write, lamb, honest, listen. (2 marks)

44. Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion, with an example of each. (3 marks)

45. Explain the difference between a common noun and a proper noun. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

46. Describe the five-finger test for choosing a book. (4 marks)

47. Give two reasons why we plan before writing a story. (2 marks)

48. Write one sentence using 'present' as a noun and one using 'present' as a verb. Show the stress with capital letters. (3 marks)

49. Compose a tongue twister with at least six words that contain the sound /w/. (3 marks)

50. Write the greeting and closing for a friendly letter to your friend Wanjiku. (2 marks)

51. Write four words with double consonants and four words with blends. (4 marks)

52. List three hygiene habits mentioned in the text. (3 marks)

53. Explain how to make the sound /r/. (3 marks)

54. Explain what the proverb 'Many hands make light work' means and give an example. (3 marks)

55. What lesson does the poem 'The Whistle' teach about winning and losing? (2 marks)

56. Fill in the double letters: di__er, ye__ow, bu__on. (3 marks)

57. Draw a mind map in words: put 'Keeping Fit' in the centre and give four branches. (4 marks)

58. Describe how you would set up a reading club in your class. (4 marks)

59. Complete the simile and explain it: 'as cold as ______'. (2 marks)

60. Punctuate: 'we planted maize beans and sorghum' (2 marks)

61. Explain why 'more better' is wrong. Give the correct form. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The first and last words on a dictionary page
   They show which words can be found on the page.

2. B — A junior encyclopaedia
   An encyclopaedia gives facts about many subjects.

3. B — Your name written in your own handwriting
   A signature shows that you agree with what is written.

4. A — girl
   Girl has the long vowel /ɜː/.

5. B — touches the ridge behind the top front teeth
   For /l/ the tongue tip touches the ridge and air flows around the sides.

6. A — Read the title and look at the pictures
   The title and pictures help you predict.

7. D — let, late
   Let and late differ in the vowel sound.

8. D — Congratulations
   Congratulations shows we are happy for someone.

9. D — look quickly for one fact
   Scanning is used to find a name, number or word.

10. D — Yours lovingly,
   Yours lovingly is friendly.

11. B — Reading smoothly with few stops
   Fluent readers read smoothly.

12. A — A newspaper
   Newspapers report news.

13. C — taller
   Short adjectives add er.

14. B — The bread was as soft as a pillow.
   It compares bread with a pillow using as ... as.

15. D — write a new message
   Compose means to write.

16. B — Words that end with the same sound
   'Wide' and 'ride' rhyme.

17. C — lying
   The letters ie change to y before -ing.

18. C — The teacher is marking our books.
   Is + verb-ing shows an action happening now.

19. B — The goat ran like the wind.
   A simile compares using like or as.

20. A — Last Saturday, my class visited a farm near our school.
   It says when, who and where.

21. B — Standing straight and looking at your audience
   Posture and eye contact show confidence.

22. B — refused
   Some children refused to play with Omondi.

23. B — Sharing blades can pass germs through blood
   He explains that blood can carry germs.

24. C — She asked where the clinic was.
   It reports a question, so it is a statement.

25. C — It may contain germs
   Boiling kills germs.

26. A — She has no soap, nor does she have water.
   After 'nor', the helping verb comes before the subject.

27. C — nor
   'Nor' follows a negative.

28. B — Face the speaker and listen for the main points
   Active listening means paying attention to the main points.

29. D — At ten o'clock.
   'When' asks for a time.

30. C — tomorrow
   'Tomorrow' is t-o-m-o-r-r-o-w.

31. C — friend
   Friend is spelt f-r-i-e-n-d.

32. D — Practising what you want to say
   Practice reduces hesitation.

33. D — The beat in the words
   Rhythm is the pattern of beats.

34. C — Tap the beat and stress the strong syllables
   Follow the beat with your voice.

35. B — The bus left.
   The past perfect shows the earlier action.

36. D — They have gone to the river.
   The participle of go is gone.

37. B — Looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number
   Scanning searches for specific information.

38. A — into
   She moved the coins to the inside.

39. D — accountant
   Accountant has a double c.

40. B — stopping
   Double the last consonant of a short verb ending in one vowel and one consonant.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A word wheel has a fixed ending and different beginning letters. You change the first letter to make a new word. With -oy you can make boy, toy and joy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixed ending, 1 mark for changing the first letter, 1 mark each for two correct words.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: b: stick first then the round part on the right. d: round part first then the stick on the right.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each letter.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: write (w), lamb (b), honest (h), listen (t)
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: A fact can be checked, such as 'The club meets on Fridays.' An opinion is what someone thinks, such as 'Saving is a good idea.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: A common noun is a general name such as 'town'. A proper noun is the special name of one person, place or thing, such as 'Kisumu', and begins with a capital letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both examples.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open the book at a page and read it. Hold up a finger for every word you do not know. Five fingers means too hard; one to three fingers is a good fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reading a page, 1 for counting unknown words with fingers, 1 for what five fingers means, 1 for what one to three fingers means.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: It puts ideas in order and makes sure we do not forget important events.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: My uncle gave me a PRE-sent. I will pre-SENT the prize to the winner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for correct stress.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: We watched worms wriggle when the wind whistled.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a sentence, 1 for at least six /w/ words, 1 for making sense.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: Dear Wanjiku, ... Yours lovingly, (your name).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the greeting with comma and 1 mark for the closing.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Double: letter, dinner, apple, bottle. Blends: train, snake, clap, flag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group of two words, up to 4.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands with soap; boil drinking water; use a clean latrine; cover food; brush teeth; cut nails short.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pull the tongue back a little and curl the tip up without touching the roof of the mouth, and round the lips slightly. The tongue tip touches nothing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for tongue pulled back, 1 mark for the tip not touching, 1 mark for rounded lips.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: It means a job is easier when many people help. For example, the whole class can sweep the compound quickly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 for a suitable example, 1 for clear expression.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: To be a good sport: lose without crying, shake hands with the other team and say 'Good try'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the lesson and 1 for a reason from the poem.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: dinner, yellow, button
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Centre: Keeping Fit. Branches: exercise, healthy food, sleep, clean water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the centre and 1 for each branch.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a day, time and place; give members roles; agree on rules such as taking turns; and read silently then share what was read.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: as cold as ice, because ice is very cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable comparison and 1 mark for the explanation.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: We planted maize, beans and sorghum.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each comma and capital/full stop.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: Better is already the comparative form, so we do not add more. The correct form is better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the reason and 1 mark for the correct form.
